questions: Are the facial movements happening involuntarily, without you trying to make them?
Do these episodes repeatedly involve forceful blinking or involuntary closing of both eyes?
Have these movements been occurring for more than a few days?
Are the movements becoming more frequent or severe?
Do bright lights, wind, stress, fatigue, or reading trigger or worsen them?
Can you temporarily suppress the movements when you concentrate?
Do you feel an urge or uncomfortable sensation that is relieved after making the movement?
Do the movements ever affect your mouth, jaw, tongue, or neck?
Are the movements limited to one side of your face?
Have you had any facial weakness, numbness, drooping, double vision, speech difficulty, or limb weakness?
Have you lost awareness, had confusion, or had any shaking of your arms or legs during these episodes?
Do you have eye pain, redness, discharge, or a persistent change in vision?
Have you recently started, stopped, or changed any medicines?
Have you recently received Botox, fillers, or another cosmetic or dental treatment involving your face?
Have you had a recent head injury, facial injury, infection, or significant emotional stress?

results: 1. Comprehensive movement-disorders neurological examination, including observation during speaking, chewing, smiling, tongue protrusion, eye opening, and sensory-trick manoeuvres
cranial nerve examination: involuntary blepharospasm with perioral and jaw dystonic spasms, provoked by speech and eating; otherwise normal
deep tendon reflexes and plantar responses: normal
distribution of the dystonia (focal, segmental, generalized): SEGMENTAL - eyelids plus perioral and jaw muscles, not isolated blepharospasm
action specificity and task dependence: spasms provoked by speech and eating
slit-lamp examination for Kayser-Fleischer rings: no rings
3. MRI of the brain with and without contrast
4. Serum ceruloplasmin, serum copper, and 24-hour urinary copper
copper / caeruloplasmin / 24 h urinary copper: normal
5. Needle electromyography of the orbicularis oculi and oromandibular muscles
needle EMG of the affected muscles: not performed
6. Therapeutic trial of botulinum toxin injections into the orbicularis oculi and affected oromandibular muscles
